title: Alice Guy-Blaché
objective: After this level you can describe the career of Alice Guy-Blaché, one of the first directors to film made-up stories.
summary: Alice Guy, Léon Gaumont's secretary, made La Fée aux choux, one of the first story films, ran Gaumont's production, then founded Solax in America; much of her credit was later lost.

cards.headline: A company secretary directed one of cinema's first story films.
cards.body: Alice Guy was hired as Léon Gaumont's secretary in Paris. Then she directed a film of her own, La Fée aux choux (The Cabbage Fairy), which Britannica dates to 1896. How did she go from taking letters to making films, and why did history nearly misplace her?

cards.headline: A fairy tale, not a train
cards.body: The Lumières filmed everyday life: workers leaving a factory, a train arriving (Level 6). Guy filmed something made up. Britannica says she is generally acknowledged as the first director to film a narrative story, and many historians hold that her fairy tale came before Méliès's story films. A few historians date it as late as 1900, though. That's why 'one of the first' is the safe way to say it.

cards.headline: Running a studio's films
cards.body: Gaumont made Guy its head of production, and she directed nearly all of the company's films until 1905. She kept experimenting, too: from 1906 to 1907 she directed short sound films using Gaumont's Chronophone. The secretary had become the person deciding what the company put on screen.

cards.headline: Her own studio, then her name forgotten
cards.body: In 1907 Guy married cameraman Herbert Blaché and moved to the United States. In 1910 she founded the Solax Company, and by 1912 it had a new, state-of-the-art studio in Fort Lee, New Jersey. Yet many of her accomplishments were later forgotten or credited to male colleagues. After she returned to France in 1922, she couldn't find work in its film industry. The films outlasted the credit.

questions.prompt: Before she began directing films, Alice Guy worked at Gaumont as _____.

options.label: a Gaumont camera operator
options.rationale: Her husband, Herbert Blaché, was the cameraman; she was hired as a secretary.

options.label: a theater pianist
options.rationale: She was hired as Gaumont's secretary, not as a pianist.

options.label: a film critic
options.rationale: She was hired as a secretary.
